newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia Lek 17 pct in foreign hands.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia Lek 17 pct in foreign hands.

text.p: Slovenian drug producer Lek, the fledgling Ljubljana bourse's star performer, said on Friday some 17 percent of its shares were held by foreign investors after a four-month long buying frenzy.
"It is hard to speculate but I think foreign ownership could soon reach some 30 percent," Marko Drazumeric, head of Lek's financial investment department, told Reuters.
The buying was largely powered by British and American investment funds, he said, citing London-based Lazard Capital Market as the third largest investor behind two local state-owned funds.
"Creditanstalt and London's Daiwa Europe are also among the major foreign buyers," he said.

Lek's share issue A has surged 74.7 percent since its flotation on September 11. Drazumeric said the share price was being driven up by a lack of willing domestic sellers and a large number of eager foreign buyers.

"Slovenian pharmaceutical companies are among the most interesting for foreign investors because of their size and profitability," Florian Hellmich, equity analyst at Investmentbank Austria in Vienna said.

On Friday, Lek's A issue was the most actively traded share on the Ljubljana bourse, jumping 6.32 percent to 24,400 tolars on volume of 11,485 shares for total turnover of 277.3 million tolars. -- Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
